power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

table.title: Common and specific gray matter abnormalities in schizophrenia and major depressive disorder: a voxel-based meta-analysis
table.statistical_tests: The analysis will be conducted using the SDM-PSI algorithm. Suitable data will be pooled and relevant information such as demographic characteristics and coordinates in standard spaces (MNI/TAL), as well as their respective t-values, will be completed. Anisotropic Gaussian kernel with 20mm (FWHM) and 2mm (voxel size) (Albajes-Eizagirre et al., 2019) will be applied. Thresholding at p ≤ .0025 uncorrected and cluster extent of k≥10 voxels will be. In line with (Radua et al., 2013), conjunction maps showing common and separate areas between schizophrenia and depression data will be generated at p ≤ .0025 uncorrected (four-tailed), k≥10 voxels and peak height=.00025. Tests for publication bias and jackknife sensitivity will be performed to check for any publication bias in our meta-analysis. Other complementary analyses will include quantitative comparative analyses to characterize the identified brain regions on the network and behavioral levels. Additionally, meta-regression (thresholded at p ≤ .0025) will be performed to rule out the effects of possible confounding variables such as age and medication status.
table.transformations: Z-values of coordinates reported from whole-brain between- group differences of will be transformed to t-values using the statistical converter (https://www.sdmproject.com/utilities/?show=Statistics).
table.inference_criteria: MNI coordinates in form of x, y, z from significant clusters of between-group differences across suitable contrasts shall be reported.
table.data_exclusion_criteria: The exclusion criteria will be as follows: (a) studies focusing entirely on participants <18 or those >60 years old, (b) studies focusing on other mental/mood disorders, (c) studies presenting ROI results only, (d) studies including findings from the same dataset as already included studies.
table.exploratory_analyses: Meta-analytic network analyses including functional characterization/decoding and meta-analytic coactivation will be performed. Other analyses including behavioral-level and molecular-level analyses will be conducted according to standard procedures. Linear model analysis will be performed to check for effects of confounding variables. Sub-group analyses on medication effects will also be performed on included studies.

table.research_questions: Schizophrenia and depression have been linked with anhedonia which may present a transdiagnostic deficits that cuts across traditional diagnostic entities. Schizophrenia is a severe and highly complex mental disorder that is characterized by heterogenous symptoms ranging from psychotic, negative and cognitive symptoms. Depression one the other hand, is a debilitating mental disorder that affects millions of people causing disabilities and morbidities every year. It is characterized by depressed mood and anhedonia (Bedwell et al., 2014; Husain and Roiser, 2018). While these two disorders are quite distinct they share dysfunctions in the domains of reward and motivational processing, in particular both disorders are characterized by persistent anhedonia. Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) is a powerful method of analyzing neuroimaging data. Previous meta-analyses have identified gray matter deficits in the frontal lobe, temporal lobe, insular and thalamus in schizophrenic patients compared to healthy controls (Torres et al., 2016; Wei et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2019). VBM studies have reported that patients with depression experience widespread local abnormalities in several brain regions such as the frontal gyrus, anterior cingulate gyrus and hippocampus (Tang et al., 2007; Wagner et al., 2008).  Against this background, we aimed to (1) Determine common brain volumetric abnormalities in patients with schizophrenia and depression, (2) Identify disorder-specific brain volume abnormalities in patients with schizophrenia compared with healthy controls (3) Identify disorder-specific brain volume abnormalities in patients with depression compared with healthy controls (4) Explore the identified brain regions on the network, behavioral, and molecular-genetic levels. Based on the previous literature, we hypothesize that both patient groups will exhibit reduced brain volumes in prefrontal regions involved in value processing and executive control. Moreover, we expected patients with schizophrenia to exhibit decreased brain volume in the thalamus, amygdala and hippocampus compared to healthy controls, while patients with depression predominately show altered prefrontal volumetric alterations.

To begin, a comprehensive literature search of VBM studies on unipolar depression will be conducted. PubMed, Web of Science and PsycInfo databases will be utilized in the literature selection process. Original case-control VBM studies in schizophrenia and depression be extracted. Suitable studies from other sources, that fulfill the inclusion criteria will be included. The literature will be screened based on titles and abstracts returned by search results. Studies written in English, published between 2000-2024. Age between 18 to 60 years old. VBM case-control studies comparing depression/schizophrenia patients versus healthy controls. Studies reporting whole-brain results in standard stereotactic space.
Only peer-reviewed, original case-control studies comparing patients and healthy controls will be included. The search criteria for the schizophrenia group includes: (rest OR resting) AND (schizophrenias OR schizophrenic disorders OR disorder, schizophrenic OR disorders, schizophrenic OR schizophrenic disorder) AND (voxel-based morphometry OR VBM). table.indices: The major aim of this work will be to identify robust gray matter abnormalities in adults with schizophrenia and major depressive disorder. To this end we will capitalize on a series of meta-analytic neuroimaging analyses using coordinate-based meta-analysis of suitable fMRI studies. The meta-analysis will be performed using the Seed-based d Mapping Permutation of Subject Images (SDM-PSI) (https://www.sdmproject.com). The analysis will be as follows; (i) Peak coordinates of between-group differences together with their effect sizes in t/z values will be acquired. All the z-values will be converted to t-values using the statistical converter. (ii) Next, the lower and upper bounds of the most probable effect size images will be estimated during the preprocessing step. (iii) The mean is computed using two algorithms, the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and meta-analysis of non-statistically significant unreported effects (MetaNSUE). This step will estimate the probable effect size and standard error as well as compute several imputations from estimates lying within the bounds.  (iv) Next, the study images which have been imputed are created. (v) Lastly, the permutation test will assess the meta-analytic images for statistical significance (Jauhar et al., 2021). The test for statistical significance test will be achieved by thresholding the obtained maps by voxel-level of p≤.0025 uncorrected.
